/*
 * GPU-accelerated AIDW interpolation algorithm 
 *
 * Implemented with / without Shared Memory
 *
 * By Dr.Gang Mei
 *
 * Created on 2015.11.06, China University of Geosciences, 
 *                        gang.mei@cugb.edu.cn
 * Revised on 2015.12.14, China University of Geosciences, 
 *                        gang.mei@cugb.edu.cn
 * 
 * Related publications:
 *  1) "Evaluating the Power of GPU Acceleration for IDW Interpolation Algorithm"
 *     http://www.hindawi.com/journals/tswj/2014/171574/
 *  2) "Accelerating Adaptive IDW Interpolation Algorithm on a Single GPU"
 *     http://arxiv.org/abs/1511.02186
 *
 * License: http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/
 */

#include <cstdio>
#include <cstdlib>     
#include <vector>
#include <cmath>
#include <chrono>
#include <cuda.h>
#include "reference.h"

// Calculate the power parameter, and then weighted interpolating
// Without using shared memory
__global__
void AIDW_Kernel(
    const float *__restrict dx, 
    const float *__restrict dy,
    const float *__restrict dz,
    const int dnum,
    const float *__restrict ix,
    const float *__restrict iy,
          float *__restrict iz,
    const int inum,
    const float area,
    const float *__restrict avg_dist) 

{
  int tid = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;
  if (tid >= inum) return;

  float sum = 0.f, dist = 0.f, t = 0.f, z = 0.f, alpha = 1.f;

  float r_obs = avg_dist[tid];                // The observed average nearest neighbor distance
  float r_exp = 0.5f / sqrtf(dnum / area);    // The expected nearest neighbor distance for a random pattern
  float R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp;                 // The nearest neighbor statistic

  // Normalize the R(S0) measure such that it is bounded by 0 and 1 by a fuzzy membership function 
  float u_R = 0.f;
  if(R_S0 >= R_min) u_R = 0.5f-0.5f * cosf(3.1415926f / R_max * (R_S0 - R_min));
  if(R_S0 >= R_max) u_R = 1.f;

  // Determine the appropriate distance-decay parameter alpha by a triangular membership function
  // Adaptive power parameter: a (alpha)
  if(u_R>= 0.f && u_R<=0.1f)  alpha = a1; 
  if(u_R>0.1f && u_R<=0.3f)  alpha = a1*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.1f)) + a2*5.f*(u_R-0.1f);
  if(u_R>0.3f && u_R<=0.5f)  alpha = a3*5.f*(u_R-0.3f) + a1*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.3f));
  if(u_R>0.5f && u_R<=0.7f)  alpha = a3*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.5f)) + a4*5.f*(u_R-0.5f);
  if(u_R>0.7f && u_R<=0.9f)  alpha = a5*5.f*(u_R-0.7f) + a4*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.7f));
  if(u_R>0.9f && u_R<=1.f)  alpha = a5;
  alpha *= 0.5f; // Half of the power

  // Weighted average
  for(int j = 0; j < dnum; j++) {
    dist = (ix[tid] - dx[j]) * (ix[tid] - dx[j]) + (iy[tid] - dy[j]) * (iy[tid] - dy[j]) ;
    t = 1.f / powf(dist, alpha);  sum += t;  z += dz[j] * t;
  }
  iz[tid] = z / sum;
}

// Calculate the power parameter, and then weighted interpolating
// With using shared memory (Tiled version of the stage 2)
__global__
void AIDW_Kernel_Tiled(
    const float *__restrict dx, 
    const float *__restrict dy,
    const float *__restrict dz,
    const int dnum,
    const float *__restrict ix,
    const float *__restrict iy,
          float *__restrict iz,
    const int inum,
    const float area,
    const float *__restrict avg_dist)
{
  // Shared Memory
  __shared__ float sdx[BLOCK_SIZE];
  __shared__ float sdy[BLOCK_SIZE];
  __shared__ float sdz[BLOCK_SIZE];

  int tid = threadIdx.x + blockIdx.x * blockDim.x; 
  if (tid >= inum) return;

  float dist = 0.f, t = 0.f, alpha = 0.f;

  int part = (dnum - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE;
  int m, e;

  float sum_up = 0.f;
  float sum_dn = 0.f;   
  float six_s, siy_s;

  float r_obs = avg_dist[tid];               //The observed average nearest neighbor distance
  float r_exp = 0.5f / sqrtf(dnum / area); // The expected nearest neighbor distance for a random pattern
  float R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp;                //The nearest neighbor statistic

  float u_R = 0.f;
  if(R_S0 >= R_min) u_R = 0.5f-0.5f * cosf(3.1415926f / R_max * (R_S0 - R_min));
  if(R_S0 >= R_max) u_R = 1.f;

  // Determine the appropriate distance-decay parameter alpha by a triangular membership function
  // Adaptive power parameter: a (alpha)
  if(u_R>= 0.f && u_R<=0.1f)  alpha = a1; 
  if(u_R>0.1f && u_R<=0.3f)  alpha = a1*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.1f)) + a2*5.f*(u_R-0.1f);
  if(u_R>0.3f && u_R<=0.5f)  alpha = a3*5.f*(u_R-0.3f) + a1*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.3f));
  if(u_R>0.5f && u_R<=0.7f)  alpha = a3*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.5f)) + a4*5.f*(u_R-0.5f);
  if(u_R>0.7f && u_R<=0.9f)  alpha = a5*5.f*(u_R-0.7f) + a4*(1.f-5.f*(u_R-0.7f));
  if(u_R>0.9f && u_R<=1.f)  alpha = a5;
  alpha *= 0.5f; // Half of the power

  float six_t = ix[tid];
  float siy_t = iy[tid];
  int lid = threadIdx.x;
  for(m = 0; m <= part; m++) {  // Weighted Sum  
    int num_threads = min(BLOCK_SIZE, dnum - BLOCK_SIZE *m);
    if (lid < num_threads) {
      sdx[lid] = dx[lid + BLOCK_SIZE * m];
      sdy[lid] = dy[lid + BLOCK_SIZE * m];
      sdz[lid] = dz[lid + BLOCK_SIZE * m];
    }
    __syncthreads();

    for(e = 0; e < BLOCK_SIZE; e++) {
      six_s = six_t - sdx[e];
      siy_s = siy_t - sdy[e];
      dist = (six_s * six_s + siy_s * siy_s);
      t = 1.f / powf(dist, alpha);  sum_dn += t;  sum_up += t * sdz[e];
    }
    __syncthreads();
  }
  iz[tid] = sum_up / sum_dn;
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  if (argc != 4) {
    printf("Usage: %s <pts> <check> <iterations>\n", argv[0]);
    printf("pts: number of points (unit: 1K)\n");
    printf("check: enable verification when the value is 1\n");
    return 1;
  }

  const int numk = atoi(argv[1]); // number of points (unit: 1K)
  const int check = atoi(argv[2]); // do check for small problem sizes
  const int iterations = atoi(argv[3]); // repeat kernel execution

  const int dnum = numk * 1024;
  const int inum = dnum;
  const size_t dnum_size = dnum * sizeof(float);
  const size_t inum_size = inum * sizeof(float);

  // Area of planar region
  const float width = 2000, height = 2000;
  const float area = width * height;

  std::vector<float> dx(dnum), dy(dnum), dz(dnum);
  std::vector<float> avg_dist(dnum);
  std::vector<float> ix(inum), iy(inum), iz(inum);
  std::vector<float> h_iz(inum);

  srand(123);
  for(int i = 0; i < dnum; i++)
  {
    dx[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 1000;
    dy[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 1000;
    dz[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 1000;
  }

  for(int i = 0; i < inum; i++)
  {
    ix[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 1000;
    iy[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 1000;
    iz[i] = 0.f;
  }

  for(int i = 0; i < dnum; i++)
  {
    avg_dist[i] = rand()/(float)RAND_MAX * 3;
  }

  printf("Size = : %d K \n", numk);
  printf("dnum = : %d\ninum = : %d\n", dnum, inum);

  if (check) {
    printf("Verification enabled\n");
    reference (dx.data(), dy.data(), dz.data(), dnum, ix.data(), 
               iy.data(), h_iz.data(), inum, area, avg_dist.data());
  } else {
    printf("Verification disabled\n");
  }

  float *d_dx, *d_dy, *d_dz;
  float *d_avg_dist;
  float *d_ix, *d_iy, *d_iz;

  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_dx, dnum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_dy, dnum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_dz, dnum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_avg_dist, dnum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_ix, inum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_iy, inum_size); 
  cudaMalloc((void**)&d_iz, inum_size); 

  cudaMemcpy(d_dx, dx.data(), dnum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 
  cudaMemcpy(d_dy, dy.data(), dnum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 
  cudaMemcpy(d_dz, dz.data(), dnum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 
  cudaMemcpy(d_avg_dist, avg_dist.data(), dnum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 
  cudaMemcpy(d_ix, ix.data(), inum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 
  cudaMemcpy(d_iy, iy.data(), inum_size, cudaMemcpyHostToDevice); 

  dim3 threadsPerBlock (BLOCK_SIZE);
  dim3 blocksPerGrid ((inum + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);

  // Weighted Interpolate using AIDW

  AIDW_Kernel<<<blocksPerGrid, threadsPerBlock>>>(
      d_dx, d_dy, d_dz, dnum, d_ix, d_iy, d_iz, inum, area, d_avg_dist);
  cudaMemcpy(iz.data(), d_iz, inum_size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost); 

  if (check) {
    bool ok = verify (iz.data(), h_iz.data(), inum, EPS);
    printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
  }

  AIDW_Kernel_Tiled<<<blocksPerGrid, threadsPerBlock>>>(
      d_dx, d_dy, d_dz, dnum, d_ix, d_iy, d_iz, inum, area, d_avg_dist);
  cudaMemcpy(iz.data(), d_iz, inum_size, cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost); 

  if (check) {
    bool ok = verify (iz.data(), h_iz.data(), inum, EPS);
    printf("%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL");
  }

  auto start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < iterations; i++)
    AIDW_Kernel<<<blocksPerGrid, threadsPerBlock>>>(
      d_dx, d_dy, d_dz, dnum, d_ix, d_iy, d_iz, inum, area, d_avg_dist);

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  auto end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  auto time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time of AIDW_Kernel       %f (s)\n", (time * 1e-9f) / iterations);

  start = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();

  for (int i = 0; i < iterations; i++)
    AIDW_Kernel_Tiled<<<blocksPerGrid, threadsPerBlock>>>(
      d_dx, d_dy, d_dz, dnum, d_ix, d_iy, d_iz, inum, area, d_avg_dist);

  cudaDeviceSynchronize();
  end = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
  time = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::nanoseconds>(end - start).count();
  printf("Average execution time of AIDW_Kernel_Tiled %f (s)\n", (time * 1e-9f) / iterations);

  cudaFree(d_dx);
  cudaFree(d_dy);
  cudaFree(d_dz);
  cudaFree(d_ix);
  cudaFree(d_iy);
  cudaFree(d_iz);
  cudaFree(d_avg_dist);
  return 0;
}

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Per thread: pre‑loop arithmetic (~33 FLOPs) plus tiled loop. The tiled loop runs 40 tiles; each tile iterates 256 times. Each inner iteration performs 5 basic ops for distance, an estimated 12 FLOPs for powf (log/exp), and 4 ops for division and accumulations, totaling ~21 FLOPs. prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: All computations use single‑precision float; no double‑precision operations are present.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel does not use half‑precision types or packed FP16 instructions; therefore FP16 FLOPs are zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Unique global data accessed: dx, dy, dz (3*dnum*4), ix, iy (2*inum*4), avg_dist (dnum*4). With dnum=inum=10240, total distinct reads = 122,880 + 81,920 + 40,960 = 245,760 bytes. All data (~286 KB) fits within the 6 MB L2 cache, so each element is fetched from DRAM only once.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each thread writes one float to iz (inum*4 = 40,960 bytes). The total write footprint (~40 KB) is far smaller than the 6 MB L2 cache, so writes remain in cache and are not flushed to DRAM during this kernel launch.

records.kernel_demangled_name: AIDW_Kernel(const float *, const float *, const float *, int, const float *, const float *, float *, int, float, const float *)

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From argv, numk=10 so dnum=inums=10*1024=10240. The first invocation of the target kernel is the explicit warm-up launch before any timing loops, using blocksPerGrid=(inum+BLOCK_SIZE-1)/BLOCK_SIZE=(10240+255)/256=40 and threadsPerBlock=BLOCK_SIZE=256.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: BLOCK_SIZE is defined as 256 in reference.h, and host code sets dim3 threadsPerBlock(BLOCK_SIZE) for the first AIDW_Kernel launch. The kernel is 1-D with no y/z dimensions specified.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: For each active thread (inum=10240), source-visible setup work is: dnum/area (1 div), sqrtf (counted as 1 FP32 op at source level), 0.5/r (1 div), r_obs/r_exp (1 div), then because avg_dist is random in [0,3], R_S0=4*avg_dist*sqrt(10240/4e6) spans about [0,0.48], so R_S0<R_max always and only the first fuzzy-cos branch can execute. Treating branch work by expected path over uniform avg_dist: all threads do the cos-branch arithmetic 4 ops + cosf 1 op, and u_R falls in [0,0.1] for 0<=R_S0<=~0.4097 (probability ~0.8536) giving no extra FP ops, or in (0.1,0.3] for ~0.1464 of threads giving 8 FP ops for the linear alpha formula; alpha*=0.5 adds 1 op always. This gives expected setup FP32 ops/thread = 3 + 5 + 0.1464*8 + 1 = 10.1712. In the j-loop (dnum=10240 iterations), each iteration performs 2 subtractions for ix-dx reused twice textually, 2 multiplications for squaring, 1 add for dist, powf counted conservatively as 1 source-level op, 1 division for 1/powf, 1 add for sum+=t, 1 multiply and 1 add for z+=dz*t, totaling 10 FP32 ops/iter; final iz=z/sum adds 1 div. Total FP32 ops/thread = 10.1712 + 10240*10 + 1 = 102411.1712, so over 10240 active threads the first invocation executes about 1,048,690,393 FP32 operations. This is a source-level estimate and likely undercounts lowered fast-math implementations of cosf, sqrtf, division, and powf.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: All floating-point variables and literals in the kernel are single precision floats, and there are no explicit double-precision operations in the source on the taken path. Although constants could be promoted internally by compilation in some cases, with the given float literals and CUDA fast-math there is no defensible source evidence for executed FP64 arithmetic.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel source uses only float data and float math functions, with no half-precision types, casts, or intrinsics. Without SASS there is no basis to attribute any compiler-generated packed FP16 arithmetic, so the defensible estimate for executed FP16 FLOPs is zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: There are 10240 active threads. Per thread, invariant arrays avg_dist, ix, and iy are each read once (3 floats = 12 B), and inside the j-loop each iteration reads dx[j], dy[j], dz[j] (12 B), for total source-level load traffic 12 + 10240*12 = 122892 B per thread; across all threads that is 1,258,414,080 B. However, DRAM traffic should reflect cache reuse: the unique read footprint of all input arrays touched by the first invocation is dx+dy+dz+ix+iy+avg_dist = 6 arrays * 10240 floats * 4 B = 245,760 B, far below the 50 MB L2, so after compulsory fills the repeated streaming over dx/dy/dz by all threads can be served from L2. Thus DRAM read is best estimated as the unique input footprint loaded once, about 245,760 B.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes exactly one float per active thread to iz[tid], so the unique output footprint is 10240*4 = 40,960 B. Because this write footprint is tiny relative to the 50 MB L2 cache and there is no evidence of eviction during this first invocation, these dirty lines can remain in write-back L2 until the subsequent cudaMemcpy or later activity, so DRAM writes during the kernel itself are best estimated as zero.

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
Let me analyze the kernel for all 10240 active threads. The kernel has two main phases: (1) computing alpha, and (2) the tiled weighted sum loop.

**Phase 1: Computing alpha (per thread, 10240 threads)**

From SASS, the pre-loop FP32 operations per thread:
- FMUL.FTZ R3, R3, R6 (dnum/area computation): 1
- MUFU.SQRT R3, R3: 1
- MUFU.RCP R6, R3: 1
- FMUL.FTZ R6, R6, 0.5: 1
- MUFU.RCP R7, R6: 1
- FMUL.FTZ R7, R4, R7: 1 (R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp)
- FSETP.GE (R7 >= 0): 1 comparison
- @P0 FMUL.FTZ R4, R7, 1.5707...: 1
- @P0 FMUL.RZ R5, R4, 0.159...: 1
- @P0 MUFU.COS R5, R5: 1
- @P0 FFMA.FTZ R4, R5, -R10, 0.5: 1 (2 FLOPs: mul+add)
- FSETP.GE (R7 >= 2): 1
- FSEL: 1
- Multiple FSETP comparisons for the alpha branches: ~8 FSETPs
- The alpha computation branches involve conditional FADD, FMUL, FFMA operations. On average, one branch is taken per thread. Looking at the SASS, the conditional operations for the taken branch involve roughly 3-4 FP ops. But since all branches are predicated (not divergent in the traditional sense), all predicated instructions execute but only the taken ones write results. However, FSEL/predicated ops still count as FP ops when they execute.

Actually, looking more carefully at the SASS, the predicated instructions (@!P2, @!P5, @!P3, @!P1) execute for threads where the predicate is true. Since threads in a warp may take different branches, all predicated paths execute for all threads (the hardware just masks writes). But for FLOP counting, we count operations that actually execute (i.e., the instruction is issued). On Hopper, predicated-off instructions still issue but don't count as FLOPs in the traditional sense. Let me count conservatively the instructions that execute.

For the alpha section, I'll count approximately: MUFU.RCP(1) + I2FP(0, int conversion) + FMUL(1) + MUFU.SQRT(1) + MUFU.RCP(1) + FMUL(1) + MUFU.RCP(1) + FMUL(1) + FSETP(1) + FMUL(1) + FMUL(1) + MUFU.COS(1) + FFMA(2) + FSETP(1) + FSEL(1) + 8 FSETPs(8) + various conditional FADD/FMUL/FFMA/FSEL. 

Let me count all FP32 instructions in the pre-loop section more carefully from SASS:
MUFU.RCP R6, UR4: 1
FMUL.FTZ R3, R3, R6: 1
MUFU.SQRT R3, R3: 1
MUFU.RCP R6, R3: 1
FMUL.FTZ R6, R6, 0.5: 1
MUFU.RCP R7, R6: 1
FMUL.FTZ R7, R4, R7: 1
FSETP.GE: 1
@P0 FMUL: 1
@P0 FMUL.RZ: 1
@P0 MUFU.COS: 1
@P0 FFMA: 2
FSETP.GE: 1
FSEL: 1
FSETP.GT: 1, FSETP.GTU: 1, FSETP.GTU: 1
PLOP3: 0 (integer)
FSETP.GE: 1, FSETP.GTU: 1, FSETP.GT: 1, FSETP.GTU: 1, FSETP.GT: 1
@!P2 FADD: 1, @!P5 FADD: 1, @!P2 FFMA: 2, @!P2 FMUL: 1
@!P3 FADD: 1, @!P1 FADD: 1
@!P2 FFMA: 2, @!P5 FFMA: 2, @!P3 FFMA: 2, @!P1 FFMA: 2
FSETP.GTU: 1, FSETP.GT: 1
@!P5 FMUL: 1, @!P3 FMUL: 1, @!P1 FMUL: 1
@!P5 FFMA: 2, @!P3 FFMA: 2, @!P1 FFMA: 2
FMUL.FTZ R3, R3, 0.5: 1
FSEL: 1

Since these are predicated, all threads in a warp issue them. For counting, I'll assume all predicated instructions execute (issue) for all threads. That gives roughly:
MUFU: 5 (RCP×3, SQRT, COS)
FMUL: 8
FFMA: 7 (each = 2 FLOPs) = 14
FADD: 4
FSETP: 12
FSEL: 2
Total pre-loop per thread ≈ 5 + 8 + 14 + 4 + 12 + 2 = 45

**Phase 2: Inner loop (tiled)**

part = (10240 - 1) / 256 = 39, so m goes from 0 to 39 (40 tiles).
Inner loop processes 8 elements per iteration (unrolled by 8), with ISETP.NE R19, 0x410 meaning 256 elements / 8 = 32 iterations of the inner loop body.

Per inner loop iteration (8 elements), from SASS:
- FADD: 16 (8 pairs of ix-dx, iy-dy subtractions)
- FMUL: 8 (squaring one component of each pair)
- FFMA: 8 (squaring other component + add to first)
- MUFU.LG2: 8
- FMUL (alpha * lg2): 8
- MUFU.EX2: 8
- FADD (sum_dn accumulation): 8 (actually 7 FADDs + 1 initial FADD)
- FFMA (sum_up accumulation): 8

Counting per inner iteration:
FADD: 16 subtractions + 7 sum_dn accumulations = let me recount from SASS...

Looking at the inner loop body (.L_x_1) more carefully for 8 elements:
FADD: R12-R3, R11-R2, R12-R27, R11-R4, R12-R23, R11-R22, R11-R6, R12-R7, R12-R5, R11-R20, R12-R3, R11-R2, R12-R21, R11-R4, R12-R6, R11-R20 = 16 FADDs for differences
FMUL: 8 (squaring first diff of each pair)
FFMA: 8 (square second diff + add) for dist computation
MUFU.LG2: 8
FMUL: 8 (alpha * lg2)
MUFU.EX2: 8
FFMA: 8 (sum_up += t * sdz[e], but actually 7 FFMAs for accumulation + 1 initial)
Looking at sum_dn: FADD R24=R22+R17(init), FADD R26=R20+R27, FADD R26+=R17, FADD R17=R26+R29, FADD R4=R17+R24, FADD R5=R4+R7, FADD R4=R5+R20, FADD R17=R4+R21 = 7 FADDs for sum_dn
And FFMA for sum_up: 8 FFMAs

So per inner iteration: 16 FADD(diff) + 8 FMUL(sq) + 8 FFMA(dist=16) + 8 LG2 + 8 FMUL(alpha*lg2) + 8 EX2 + 7 FADD(sum_dn) + 8 FFMA(sum_up=16) + 1 FSETP
= 16+8+16+8+8+8+7+16+1 = 88 FP32 ops per inner iteration

32 inner iterations per tile × 40 tiles = 1280 inner iterations per thread.
Inner loop FLOPs per thread = 1280 × 88 = 112,640

Post-loop: MUFU.RCP + FMUL = 2 FLOPs

Total per thread ≈ 45 + 112,640 + 2 = 112,687
Total FP32 FLOPs = 10240 × 112,687 ≈ 1,153,914,880

So iterations = (0x410 - 0x10) / 0x20 = 0x400/0x20 = 32 iterations, processing 32×8 = 256 elements per tile. This matches BLOCK_SIZE=256.

Total FP32 ≈ 10240 × (45 + 32 × 40 × 88 + 2) = 10240 × (45 + 112640 + 2) = 10240 × 112687 ≈ 1,153,914,880

records.kernel_demangled_name: AIDW_Kernel(const float *, const float *, const float *, int, const float *, const float *, float *, int, float, const float *)

prediction.blockSz_explanation: BLOCK_SIZE is defined as 256, so threadsPerBlock is (256, 1, 1).
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
All 10240 threads are active (40*256 = 10240 = inum). Per thread analysis:

**Pre-loop section (computing alpha):**
- r_exp = 0.5f / sqrtf(dnum / area): dnum/area is a float div (1), sqrtf (1), divide 0.5/result (1) = 3 ops
- R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp: 1 div = 1 op
- u_R computation with cosf: 0.5f - 0.5f * cosf(3.1415926f / R_max * (R_S0 - R_min)): sub (1), div by R_max (1), mul (1), cosf (1 source-level), mul 0.5*cos (1), sub 0.5-result (1) = 6 ops (cosf expands to many HW instructions but counting source-level)
- The alpha if-chain: depending on which branch is taken, roughly 5-10 ops per branch. On average ~8 ops for the multiplication/addition expressions.
- alpha *= 0.5f: 1 mul

Conservatively, pre-loop: ~19 source-level FP32 ops per thread (not counting cosf/sqrtf expansion).

**Inner loop (j=0 to dnum-1 = 10239), per iteration:**
- ix[tid] - dx[j]: 1 sub
- squared: 1 mul
- iy[tid] - dy[j]: 1 sub
- squared: 1 mul
- addition of two squares: 1 add
- powf(dist, alpha): 1 source-level call
- 1.f / powf result: 1 div
- sum += t: 1 add
- dz[j] * t: 1 mul
- z += ...: 1 add
= 10 source-level FP32 ops per iteration

**Post-loop:**
- iz[tid] = z / sum: 1 div

Loop body: 10 * 10240 = 102400 ops per thread
Pre-loop: ~19 ops per thread
Post-loop: 1 op per thread

Total source-level per thread: ~102420

However, powf and cosf and sqrtf expand into many FP32 instructions at the hardware level. With -use_fast_math, powf(x,y) typically expands to __logf + mul + __expf, which is roughly 10-20 FP32 instructions. sqrtf maps to a MUFU instruction (~1-2 ops). cosf maps to MUFU + a few ops (~5-10).

For powf with fast math: approximately 2 MUFU ops + several FMUL/FADD/FMA, roughly ~10 FP32 ops per call. With 10240 iterations per thread, that's significant.

Estimating powf as ~10 FP32 ops: 10240 * 10 = 102400 additional per thread from powf expansion.
sqrtf: ~2 ops, cosf: ~8 ops.

Revised per thread: pre-loop ~29 ops, loop = 10240 * (9 + 10 for powf) = 10240 * 19 ≈ 194560, post-loop = 1.
Total per thread: ~194590

Total across 10240 threads: 194590 * 10240 ≈ 1,992,601,600

Rounding to a reasonable estimate: ~1,992,601,600 FP32 FLOPs. But given uncertainty in powf expansion, I'll estimate conservatively at the source level first: 10240 * (19 + 10*10240 + 1) = 10240 * 102420 = 1,048,780,800 source-level FP32 ops, plus transcendental expansions adding roughly another ~1 billion. Total estimate: ~2,000,000,000.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: No double-precision operations are present in the kernel. All arithmetic is single-precision float.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: No half-precision operations are present in the kernel source. The compiler may insert a small number of HFMA2 instructions for constant materialization on sm_86, but this is uncertain without SASS. Estimating 0 conservatively.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation:
Each thread reads: avg_dist[tid] (4B), ix[tid] (4B), iy[tid] (4B) = 12 bytes of per-thread data. Total unique: 10240 * 12 = 122,880 bytes.

In the inner loop, each thread reads dx[j], dy[j], dz[j] for j=0..10239. These arrays are each 10240*4 = 40,960 bytes. Total for 3 arrays: 122,880 bytes. These are read by all threads, so the unique footprint is 122,880 bytes for the data arrays.

Total unique read footprint: 122,880 (avg_dist) + 40,960 (ix) + 40,960 (iy) + 40,960 (dx) + 40,960 (dy) + 40,960 (dz) = 245,760 bytes.

The L2 cache is 5 MB, so the entire read footprint (245,760 bytes ≈ 240 KB) fits easily in L2. However, these are cold reads on first invocation, so all unique data must be fetched from DRAM once. The DRAM read is approximately equal to the unique footprint: ~245,760 bytes. With cache line granularity (128-byte sectors for GDDR6X), the data is contiguous so there's minimal waste. Rounding to cache line boundaries: each array of 10240 floats = 40960 bytes = 320 cache lines of 128 bytes = 40960 bytes exactly. So 6 arrays * 40960 = 245,760 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes iz[tid] for each of the 10240 threads: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes. The total write footprint is 40,960 bytes which easily fits in the 5 MB L2 cache. Since the L2 is write-back, these dirty cache lines will remain in L2 and not be evicted to DRAM during this kernel invocation. Therefore DRAM bytes written is approximately 0.

records.kernel_demangled_name: AIDW_Kernel_Tiled(const float *, const float *, const float *, int, const float *, const float *, float *, int, float, const float *)

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From host code with argv = `10 1 100`, `numk=10`, so `dnum=inum=10*1024=10240`. The target kernel’s first invocation is the standalone `AIDW_Kernel_Tiled<<<blocksPerGrid,threadsPerBlock>>>` after the first non-tiled kernel and verification, with `BLOCK_SIZE=256` and `blocksPerGrid=(10240+255)/256=40`.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: `threadsPerBlock` is constructed directly as `dim3(BLOCK_SIZE)` and `BLOCK_SIZE` is defined in `reference.h` as 256. The kernel is 1-D and SASS uses only `SR_CTAID.X` and `SR_TID.X`, confirming a 1-D launch of 256 threads per block.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: For the first tiled-kernel invocation, 10240 threads execute. Per thread, setup before the tiled loop does about 31 FP32 ops on the taken non-transcendental path (r_exp/r_obs/R_S0, u_R computation, alpha piecewise interpolation, final alpha*=0.5), plus transcendental/lowered work evidenced by SASS: sqrt as `RCP+FMUL+SQRT+RCP`, cos as `FMUL+FMUL+COS+FFMA`, and the final division as `RCP+FMUL`; with random `avg_dist in [0,3)`, `R_S0` is always >=2 for these constants, so `u_R=1` and alpha path collapses to `alpha=1.75`, meaning no piecewise FFMA path executes except predicates/selects. In the main work, source iterates `m=0..39` and inner `e=0..255`, so every live thread executes 40*256=10240 stencil evaluations; SASS shows each evaluation computing `dist` with 2 FADD + 1 FMUL + 1 FFMA, then `powf(dist,alpha)` lowered to `LG2+FMUL+EX2`, accumulation `sum_dn += t` as 1 FADD, and `sum_up += t*sdz[e]` as 1 FFMA, totaling 9 FP32 ops/evaluation. Thus FP32 FLOPs = 10240 threads * (setup 42 + loop 10240*9) = 943104000.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel arguments and all arithmetic are single-precision `float`, and the SASS contains no double-precision arithmetic instructions (no DADD/DMUL/DFMA/etc.) on the executed path. Therefore the first invocation performs no FP64 FLOPs.

So: dnum/area = 1 (the int dnum is converted to float, then divided by area float), sqrtf = 1, 0.5f/sqrt = ~2 (rcp+mul) → ~4 ops.

- avg_dist[tid]: 1 float = 4 bytes (unique footprint: 10240 × 4 = 40,960 bytes)
- ix[tid]: 1 float = 4 bytes (40,960 bytes)
- iy[tid]: 1 float = 4 bytes (40,960 bytes)
- In the inner loop (10240 iterations): dx[j], dy[j], dz[j] each read once per j. These are the same arrays accessed by all threads. Unique footprint: 3 × 10240 × 4 = 122,880 bytes.

Total unique read footprint: 40,960 × 3 + 122,880 = 245,760 bytes ≈ 240 KB.

This easily fits in the 50 MB L2 cache. However, these are cold reads (first invocation), so all unique data must be fetched from DRAM once. The data was copied via cudaMemcpy before the kernel, so it's likely already in L2 from the memcpy. But cudaMemcpy transfers are typically large enough that the L2 may have evicted some. Given the total data is only ~240 KB which is tiny compared to 50 MB L2, the cudaMemcpy data should still be resident in L2.

Actually, the cudaMemcpy operations transfer: dx(40KB) + dy(40KB) + dz(40KB) + avg_dist(40KB) + ix(40KB) + iy(40KB) = 240KB total. This all fits in L2 easily, so the kernel reads would all hit L2 cache.

DRAM bytes read ≈ 0 since all data fits in L2 from the prior cudaMemcpy operations. But to be safe, the memcpy itself would have loaded data into L2. The kernel's first invocation would find all data in L2.

However, if we consider that the data must have been written to DRAM by cudaMemcpy and then read back, the conservative answer is that the kernel reads ~245,760 bytes from DRAM. But since L2 is 50MB and total working set is ~240KB, it's very likely all in L2. I'll estimate 0 DRAM reads for the kernel itself.

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
All 10240 threads are active (40*256 = 10240 = inum). Per thread:

**Pre-loop (alpha computation):**
- r_exp = 0.5f / sqrtf(dnum / area): dnum/area is 1 FP32 div, sqrtf is 1 FP32 op, 0.5f/ is 1 FP32 div = ~3 ops. With -use_fast_math, sqrtf maps to MUFU.RSQ + FMUL (2 ops), and divisions map to MUFU.RCP + FMUL (2 ops each). So: dnum/area → 2 ops, sqrtf → 2 ops, 0.5f/sqrt → 2 ops = 6 ops.
- R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp: 2 ops (RCP+MUL with fast math).
- u_R computation: cosf with fast math → MUFU.COS + a few setup ops. The expression 3.1415926f/R_max*(R_S0-R_min) = pi/2*R_S0: 1 mul (pi/2 is const), then 0.5f-0.5f*cos(...): 1 MUFU.COS + 1 mul + 1 sub = ~3 ops. Plus the multiply by const: total ~4 ops for u_R.
- Alpha computation: depends on which branch is taken. Each branch has ~8-10 FP32 ops. On average ~9 ops per thread. Plus alpha *= 0.5f: 1 mul. Total alpha section: ~10 ops.
- Total pre-loop: ~22 ops per thread.

**Inner loop:** part = (10240-1)/256 = 39, so m goes 0..39, 40 iterations. Inner loop e goes 0..255, 256 iterations. Total inner iterations = 40*256 = 10240 per thread.

Per inner iteration:
- six_s = six_t - sdx[e]: 1 sub
- siy_s = siy_t - sdy[e]: 1 sub
- dist = six_s*six_s + siy_s*siy_s: 2 mul + 1 add = 3 ops (or 1 FMA + 1 MUL = 2 ops with FMA)
- powf(dist, alpha): with -use_fast_math, powf is __powf which uses __logf + mul + __expf. __logf → MUFU.LG2 (1 op), mul by alpha (1 op), __expf → MUFU.EX2 (1 op) = 3 ops.
- t = 1.f / powf(...): with fast math, RCP + MUL or just MUFU.RCP = ~1-2 ops. Let's say 2 ops (RCP + MUL).
- sum_dn += t: 1 add
- sum_up += t * sdz[e]: 1 FMA (or 1 mul + 1 add = 2 ops). With FMA: 2 ops (mul+add counted as 2 FLOPs in FMA).

Per inner iteration: 1+1+3+3+2+1+1+1 = let me recount carefully:
- 2 subs, dist = FMA(six_s, six_s, 0) then FMA(siy_s, siy_s, dist) = 2 FMA = 4 ops, or mul+mul+add = 3 ops. With compiler: likely 1 MUL + 1 FMA = 3 ops.
- powf: 3 ops (LG2 + MUL + EX2)
- 1/powf: 1 RCP = 1 op (MUFU.RCP)
- sum_dn += t: 1 FADD
- sum_up += t*sdz[e]: 1 FMA = 2 ops

Total per inner iteration: 2 + 3 + 3 + 1 + 1 + 2 = 12 ops.

Per thread inner loop total: 10240 * 12 = 122,880 ops.

**Post-loop:** iz[tid] = sum_up / sum_dn: with fast math = 2 ops (RCP+MUL).

Per thread total: ~22 + 122,880 + 2 = ~122,904 ops.
Total: 10240 * 122,904 ≈ 1,258,537,000. Let me be more precise: 10240 * 122,904 = 1,258,536,960.

However, the exact count depends heavily on compiler optimizations. I'll estimate ~1,258,537,000 FP32 FLOPs.

- Loading ix, iy: 0 FP ops
- HFMA2 at 0x00b0: This is an FP16 instruction, counted separately.

The loop iterates `part+1` times where `part = (dnum-1)/BLOCK_SIZE = (10240-1)/256 = 39`, so 40 iterations.

- FADD (subtract iy-sdy[e]): 1  
- FMUL (six_s * six_s): 1
- FFMA (+ siy_s * siy_s): 1 → dist
- MUFU.LG2 (log2(dist)): 1
- FMUL (alpha * log2(dist)): 1
- MUFU.EX2 (2^(-alpha*log2)): 1 → t = 1/pow(dist,alpha)
- FADD (sum_dn += t): 1
- FFMA (sum_up += t * sdz[e]): 1

Per tile iteration: 256 * 9 = 2304 FP32 ops
Over 40 tiles: 40 * 2304 = 92160 FP32 ops per thread

**Post-loop:**
- MUFU.RCP (1/sum_dn): 1
- FMUL (sum_up * (1/sum_dn)): 1
Total: 2 FP32 ops per thread

**Total for all threads:** 10240 * 92194 = 944,066,560

However, looking more carefully at the SASS, the I2F at 0x00a0 converts int to float (1 FP32 op). Let me also count that.

- ix[tid]: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes  
- iy[tid]: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes
- dx[0..10239]: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes (loaded into shared memory, each element loaded once across all tiles)
- dy[0..10239]: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes
- dz[0..10239]: 10240 * 4 = 40,960 bytes

DRAM reads will be minimal or zero. However, to be conservative, the first kernel may have evicted some data. Given the small footprint relative to L2, I estimate DRAM reads ≈ 0 bytes (all served from L2 cache from the previous kernel's loads).

Actually, the previous kernel (AIDW_Kernel) read the same arrays, so they should be warm in L2. But to be safe, let's assume compulsory misses for the unique footprint: 245,760 bytes. Given L2 is 40MB and total footprint is ~240KB, all data fits easily.

prediction.fp32_flop_explanation:
There are 10240 active threads (inum=10240, grid=40*256=10240, all pass the bounds check).

Per thread, analyzing the SASS:

**Pre-loop section (alpha computation):**
- FMUL.FTZ R4, R4, R5 (1)
- MUFU.SQRT R4 (1)
- MUFU.RCP R5 (1) [for r_exp computation]
- FMUL.FTZ R5, R5, 0.5 (1)
- MUFU.RCP R5 (1)
- FMUL.FTZ R6, R2, R5 (1) [R_S0 = r_obs / r_exp]
- MUFU.RCP R5 at 0x00a0 (1) [for dnum/area]
- I2FP (conversion, not FP op)

Conditional cosf path (R_S0 >= 0 which is almost always true for random positive avg_dist):
- FMUL.FTZ R7 (1)
- FMUL.RZ R3 (1)
- MUFU.COS R3 (1)
- FFMA.FTZ R2 (2 - multiply + add)

Then FSEL (not counted as FLOP).

Alpha computation - the conditional branches. Each thread takes exactly one of the 6 alpha paths. The SASS shows all conditions are evaluated with predicated instructions. Counting all predicated FP instructions that execute regardless of predicate (on Ampere, predicated-off instructions don't execute FLOPs). However, the compiler uses FSETP comparisons and predicated arithmetic. Let me count the FSETP and arithmetic:

FSETPs: ~10 FSETP instructions (these are comparisons, counted as FP ops)
Predicated arithmetic: Each thread executes only the instructions for its specific alpha branch. On average, looking at the branches, each has roughly 3-5 FP ops. But since all predicated instructions are issued, on Ampere predicated-off instructions are not counted as FLOPs.

Let me carefully count the FSETP instructions (each is 1 FP32 op):
0x01f0, 0x0200, 0x0210, 0x0230, 0x0240, 0x0250, 0x0280, 0x02a0, 0x02b0, 0x02c0, 0x0350, 0x03e0, 0x01c0 = 13 FSETPs

FMUL.FTZ R2, R2, 0.5 at 0x0480 (1) - always executes
FSEL at 0x0490 (not FP)

For the alpha branches, conservatively each thread executes one branch. The branches have varying numbers of ops. Since avg_dist is random [0,3), and the alpha computation depends on u_R, the distribution varies. For a rough estimate, I'll count the average predicated FP ops per thread as ~6 (FADD, MOV-as-immediate, FFMA, FMUL, FFMA pattern).

Pre-loop total per thread: ~3 MUFU.RCP + 1 MUFU.SQRT + 1 MUFU.COS + ~5 FMUL/FFMA/FADD + 13 FSETP + ~6 alpha branch ops + 1 final FMUL = ~30 FP32 ops

**Inner loop (dnum=10240 iterations):**
The SASS shows the loop is unrolled 4x (labels .L_x_5). Per 4 iterations:
- 4× FADD (iy-dy): 4
- 4× FADD (ix-dx): 4
- 4× FMUL (dy_diff²): 4
- 4× FFMA (dx_diff² + dy_diff²): 4
- 4× MUFU.LG2: 4
- 4× FMUL (alpha*lg2): 4
- 4× MUFU.EX2 (-neg): 4 (the negation of R27 etc. counts as FNEG = 1 each, but in SASS it's folded into EX2 operand modifier, so 0 extra)
- 4× FADD (sum += t): 4
- 4× FFMA (z += dz*t): 4

Per iteration: 8 ops (2 FADD + 1 FMUL + 1 FFMA + 1 LG2 + 1 FMUL + 1 EX2 + 1 FADD + 1 FFMA) = 9 FP32 ops per iteration.

Wait, let me recount per iteration from the unrolled block:
FADD (iy-dy), FADD (ix-dx), FMUL (sq), FFMA (sq+sq), MUFU.LG2, FMUL (alpha*lg2), MUFU.EX2, FADD (sum), FFMA (z accum) = 9 ops per iteration.

But the negation in MUFU.EX2 -R27: the source modifier is a negation. On NVIDIA GPUs, source operand modifiers (negation) are free and not counted as separate FLOPs.

So 9 FP32 ops per inner iteration × 10240 iterations = 92160 per thread.

Post-loop: MUFU.RCP R5, R14 (1) + FMUL.FTZ R5, R5, R12 (1) = 2 ops.

Total per thread: ~30 + 92160 + 2 = 92192
Total: 92192 × 10240 ≈ 944,046,080

FMUL.FTZ (0x00f0): 1
MUFU.SQRT (0x0100): 1
MUFU.RCP (0x0110): 1
FMUL.FTZ (0x0120): 1
MUFU.RCP (0x0130): 1
FMUL.FTZ (0x0140): 1
FSETP.GE (0x0160): 1

Conditional (P0 = R_S0 >= 0, true for positive values):
FMUL.FTZ (0x0170): 1
FMUL.RZ (0x0190): 1
MUFU.COS (0x01a0): 1
FFMA.FTZ (0x01b0): 2 (mul+add)

FSETP.GE (0x01c0): 1
13 more FSETPs: let me count exactly from 0x01f0 to 0x03e0: 0x01f0, 0x0200, 0x0210, 0x0230, 0x0240, 0x0250, 0x0280, 0x02a0, 0x02b0, 0x02c0, 0x0350, 0x03e0 = 12

FMUL at 0x0480: 1

For alpha branch ops, assuming average ~5 predicated FP ops execute per thread.

Pre-loop: 7 (non-conditional) + 5 (conditional cosf) + 1 + 12 (FSETPs) + 1 + 5 (alpha branch) = 31

Total per thread: 31 + 9*10240 + 2 = 92193
Total: 92193 * 10240 = 944,048,320

Rounding, approximately 944,048,320 FP32 FLOPs.

For dx, dy, dz: each is 40,960 bytes. All 10240 threads read the same dx/dy/dz arrays, so the unique footprint is 40,960 bytes each. These will be loaded from DRAM once and cached.

(1 div), R_S0=r_obs/r_exp (1 div); u_R path conservatively assumes the cosine branch executes for all threads, giving (R_S0-R_min) 1 sub, (pi/R_max) 1 div, multiply by previous term 1 mul, 0.5f*cosf(...) 1 mul, 0.5f-... 1 sub; fuzzy-alpha selection depends on data, so I use the first interval (u_R<=0.1) as the most defensible deterministic path from the seeded random inputs, which adds only alpha*=0.5f (1 mul). In the j-loop with dnum=10240 iterations, each iteration does (ix-dx) and (iy-dy): 2 subs, two squarings: 2 muls, add: 1 add, t=1/powf(dist,alpha): powf counted source-level as 1 plus reciprocal div 1, sum+=t: 1 add, z+=dz[j]*t: 1 mul + 1 add, totaling 10 FLOPs/iter; final iz=z/sum adds 1 div. Total per thread = 6 + 5 + 1 + 10240*10 + 1 = 102413 FP32 FLOPs, and over 10240 threads this is 1,048,709,120 FP32 FLOPs. This is source-level and likely undercounts lowered fast-math implementations of sqrtf/cosf/powf/div.
metrics_explanations.fp64_flop_explanation: All arithmetic variables and constants used in the kernel are float, and there are no explicit double operations in the source. Therefore the first invocation performs no FP64 FLOPs by source analysis.
metrics_explanations.fp16_flop_explanation: The kernel source uses only single-precision float data and no half types or half intrinsics. Without SASS evidence of compiler-generated packed FP16 helper instructions, the defensible estimate is zero FP16 FLOPs.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_read_explanation: For the first invocation, each of 10240 threads reads avg_dist[tid], ix[tid], and iy[tid] once plus scans dx[j], dy[j], and dz[j] for all 10240 j values. The unique global-memory footprint touched by this kernel is dx,dy,dz,ix,iy,avg_dist = 6 arrays * 10240 floats * 4 B = 245,760 B, which is far smaller than the 6 MB L2, so a defensible DRAM estimate is one compulsory fetch of that footprint with subsequent reuses served from cache; total source-level load traffic is much larger but should not all reach DRAM.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread writes one float to iz[tid], so the unique output footprint is 10240 * 4 B = 40,960 B. Because this write footprint is tiny relative to the 6 MB L2 and there is no evidence of eviction during this first invocation, the stores can remain dirty in L2, so DRAM writes during the kernel are estimated as zero.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From host code, dnum = inum = numk*1024 with command-line args 10 1 100, so inum = 10240. The first invocation of the target tiled kernel is launched once before the timing loop with blocksPerGrid = ceil(10240/256) = 40.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: BLOCK_SIZE is a compile-time macro set to 256 in reference.h, and host code uses dim3 threadsPerBlock(BLOCK_SIZE). Thus the first tiled-kernel launch uses 256 threads in x and 1 in y/z.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: For each active thread, setup before the tiled loop executes about 21 FP32 arithmetic ops visible in source/SASS on the taken straight-line path: dnum/area, sqrt reciprocal scaling, r_obs/r_exp, fuzzy-membership arithmetic (assuming R_S0<2 so cos path executes and the later clamp does not), alpha piecewise selection taken as the default u_R<=0.1 case plus alpha*=0.5, and final output division. In the main work, the SASS shows the inner e-loop fully unrolled for 256 entries per tile and repeated for 40 tiles; per data point it performs 2 subtracts + 2 multiplies + 1 add for dist, then powf(dist,alpha) lowered by fast-math into LG2, multiply-by-alpha, EX2 plus reciprocal accumulation/use, and accumulates sum_dn and sum_up, totaling about 12 FP32 FLOPs per j, so total FP32 FLOPs = 10240 threads * (21 + 10240*12) = 1,258,700,800.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel source uses only float data and float math (sqrtf, cosf, powf), and the supplied SASS contains no double-precision DADD/DMUL/DFMA-style instructions on the executed path. Therefore the first invocation performs no FP64 arithmetic.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: There are no half-precision source datatypes or packed half arithmetic instructions in the provided SASS for this kernel. All arithmetic is performed in single precision, so FP16 FLOPs are zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The target kernel is first invoked after a prior untiled AIDW_Kernel launch and a device-to-host copy of d_iz, but the tiled kernel's own read working set is small enough to fit in the 5 MB L2: unique global reads are dx/dy/dz (3*10240 floats), ix/iy/avg_dist (3*10240 floats), totaling 6*10240*4 = 245,760 bytes. Because the tiled kernel reuses dx/dy/dz through shared-memory tiling and repeatedly reuses ix/iy per thread, DRAM read traffic for this invocation is best estimated by that unique footprint rather than raw total loads.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each active thread writes one float iz[tid], so the unique global store footprint is 10240*4 = 40,960 bytes. Since this is far smaller than the 5 MB L2 and there is no evidence of eviction pressure within this invocation, those writes can remain dirty in L2, so DRAM bytes written during the kernel itself are estimated as zero.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: The host code computes blocksPerGrid = (inum + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE. With numk=10, dnum=inum=10240 and BLOCK_SIZE=256, blocksPerGrid = 40, so the first launch uses a 1‑D grid of 40 blocks.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: BLOCK_SIZE is defined as 256 and used as the thread block dimension. No y/z dimensions are specified, so the launch uses (256,1,1) threads per block.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: Per thread: ~21 FP32 ops for the scalar pre‑loop work (sqrtf, division, cosf, conditional arithmetic, alpha scaling). The inner loop runs dnum=10240 times; each iteration does 5 ops for distance, ~10 ops for powf, 1 division, 1 add to sum, and 2 ops for z accumulation → ~19 ops. Total per thread = 21 + 10240*19 = 194,581 FP32 FLOPs. With 10240 threads, total FP32 FLOPs ≈ 1.99e9.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: The kernel uses only float (FP32) arithmetic; no double‑precision variables or operations appear.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: No half‑precision types or intrinsics are used in the kernel, so FP16 FLOPs are zero.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Unique global data accessed: dx, dy, dz (3*10240*4 = 122,880 B), avg_dist (10240*4 = 40,960 B), ix and iy (2*10240*4 = 81,920 B). Total unique footprint ≈ 245,760 B, which fits comfortably in the 40 MiB L2 cache, so after the first compulsory miss the rest are served from cache. Hence DRAM reads ≈ 245,760 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each thread writes one float to iz[tid] (10240*4 = 40,960 B). The write set also fits in L2, and the cache is write‑back, so no write‑back to DRAM occurs during this kernel launch. DRAM writes are therefore estimated as 0.
